- Requirement: "the consumer wrapper listens to every workflow ("*") and skips the pipeline's own AI … workflows" (PR Description; restated in `workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml` lines 14–22)
  Expected change site: `workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml` `workflow_run` trigger
  Evidence of absence: The file declares `workflows: ["*"]` (line 18 in the inlined PR diff). In GitHub Actions the `workflows` key on `workflow_run` is a literal workflow-name allowlist; `"*"` matches only a workflow literally named `*`, which does not exist in any consumer. To match every completed workflow the `workflows` key must be omitted entirely (`workflow_run: { types: [completed] }`), and the `if:` predicate then continues to filter out `AI …` workflows. The accompanying test at `tests/test_ci_failure_workflow_run_triggers.py:113` asserts `assert _on(data)["workflow_run"] == {"workflows": ["*"], "types": ["completed"]}`, codifying the broken behaviour. Editor summary in PR comment entry[13] claims to have "omitted the workflow-name allowlist" in `workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml:14-19`, but the current file in the PR diff still shows `workflows: ["*"]`, so the consumer wrapper never receives a `workflow_run` event for any real workflow and Q55 is unimplemented.

  SEVERITY: BLOCKER

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- Requirement: "the consumer wrapper listens to every workflow ("*") and skips the pipeline's own AI … workflows" (PR Description, Q55). The consumer wrapper's `triage-workflow-run` job must trigger on every completed workflow in a consumer repo except the pipeline's own `AI …` workflows.
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml line 18 (`workflow_run` trigger) and tests/test_ci_failure_workflow_run_triggers.py line 118 (the assertion that pins the trigger shape).
  Evidence of absence: The consumer wrapper at workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml:18 uses `workflows: ["*"]`. In GitHub Actions, the `workflow_run.workflows` filter is a name allowlist that accepts workflow names or file paths — it does NOT support `*` as a wildcard. A literal `["*"]` matches only a workflow literally named `*`, which no consumer repo has. To match all workflows the `workflows` key must be omitted entirely from the `workflow_run` trigger. The test at tests/test_ci_failure_workflow_run_triggers.py:118 pins the broken behavior: `assert _on(data)["workflow_run"] == {"workflows": ["*"], "types": ["completed"]}`. The editor summary in PR comment entry[13] (2026-10-05T08:02:06Z) explicitly confirmed this: "The finding is valid: `workflows` is a name allowlist, while omitting it selects all workflows. I'm removing the literal `*` filter." However, the fix was never committed — the LAST RUN DIFF contains only relay changes, and the file on disk still has `workflows: ["*"]`. As a result, no consumer repo will ever receive a `workflow_run` event for any of its workflows, so the `triage-workflow-run` job never fires, and CI failures in consumer repos remain untriaged — the exact problem this PR set out to fix.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
